messages.content: Write the design philosophy section of an API's public documentation. Around 200 words.

output:
No specific API was named, so this is written as a drop-in section any JSON/HTTP API can adapt — swap the concrete choices (cursor pagination, RFC 3339, NDJSON) for whatever yours actually does.

---

## Design philosophy

Every endpoint follows a few rules we haven't broken since v1.

**Nouns, then verbs.** Resources have stable URLs. What you can do to them lives in the HTTP method, not in an `?action=` parameter. If you can guess the URL for something you haven't read about yet, we got this right.

**One obvious way.** Where two designs both worked, we shipped one. There is no second pagination style, no alternate date format, no legacy field kept alive out of politeness. Requests carry JSON, timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC, and lists page by opaque cursor.

**Errors are part of the contract.** A 4xx response names the field that was wrong and says what would have been accepted. We treat a confusing error message as a bug and fix it like one.

**Boring beats clever.** No client library is required. curl and a JSON parser get you everything, including streaming, which is newline-delimited JSON over a long-lived connection.

**Additions, not surprises.** We add fields and enum values without warning, so parse leniently and ignore what you don't recognize. We never remove or repurpose one inside a major version. Breaking changes get a new version number and a year of overlap.
